questionText: [Set 45.30] In India, the 'AGMARK' certification mark issued by the Directorate of Marketing and Inspection is mandatory for certifying the quality of:

options.text: Industrial manufactured electronics and household electrical appliances (ISI)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Gold and precious silver jewellery items (Hallmark)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Processed fruit juices, jams, and pickles (FPO/FSSAI)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

options.text: Agricultural food products and commodities (such as ghee, honey, butter, and spices)
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for Standardization Marks in India: AGMARK.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Standardization Marks in India: AGMARK (Resource Management):
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT Class 12 Home_Science (Consumer Education and Protection - Standardization Marks in India: AGMARK):
AGMARK is a certification mark for agricultural products in India, assuring conformity to a set of standards approved by the Directorate of Marketing and Inspection (DMI).

Hence, Option (B) is the correct answer.

Therefore, option (D) is the correct answer.

questionText:
Match the consumer exploitation issue in List I with its manifestation in List II:

List I:
(A) Food Adulteration
(B) Weights and Measures Fraud
(C) Misleading Advertising
(D) Spurious / Duplicate Goods

List II:
(I) Adding papaya seeds to black pepper or water and starch to fresh milk
(II) Using hollow-bottomed weights, bent balance beams, or uncalibrated electronic scales
(III) Claiming a cosmetic cream permanently alters skin color in 3 days with zero side effects
(IV) Selling substandard counterfeit counterfeit electronics under trademarked brand logos

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Correctly maps each entity across columns.

options.text: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Adulteration dilutes quality; Weights fraud shorts quantity; Misleading ads make false claims; Spurious goods forge authentic brands.
Hence Option D is correct.
Hence, option (B) is the correct match.
